sixLiteralCanonicalGroups.individualGround: NPS explicitly ranks polar bears as the largest living bear SPECIES. Kodiak is Ursus arctos middendorffi, a brown-bear subspecies, with regional/sex/season size variability. Overlapping individual weight ranges or a Kodiak skull record do not make every Kodiak smaller/larger or establish a contradictory species rank. No global average, universal pairwise ordering or record-body-mass calculation is invented. Four distinct living bear-species labels give one conventional species-rank key; no separate Kodiak-species option is fabricated.
